extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent owners, and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) filing appeals or cross-appeals to the USPTO Board (ex parte and inter partes reexamination)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and content/format/time/fee rules for notices of appeal, briefs, reply briefs, examiner answers, oral hearings, decisions, rehearings, and post-decision actions in ex parte and inter partes patent appeals to the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may appeal and timing for filing notice of appeal (§41.31 / §41.61)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every applicant any of whose claims has been twice rejected (or owner in specified reexamination circumstances) may appeal by filing a notice of appeal accompanied by the fee set forth in §41.20(b)(1) within the time period provided under §1.134 (or the Right of Appeal Notice for inter partes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to applicants in national applications, reissue applicants, and owners in ex parte reexamination (differences depending on filing date of reexamination). Notices of appeal or cross appeal must identify appealed claims and be signed. Time periods for notices of appeal in inter partes may not be extended; for ex parte certain time periods are extendable under cited sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement exception for notices of appeal (§41.31(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The signature requirement of §1.33 of this title does not apply to a notice of appeal filed under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of appeal still must comply with other identification/signature requirements in the relevant sections (e.g., inter partes requires signed notices by owner/requester or authorized attorney/agent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of appeal – which rejections are appealed (§41.31(c) / §41.61(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal must be taken from the rejection of all claims under rejection which the applicant or owner proposes to contest; similarly, an appeal/cross appeal must be taken from all rejections or determinations favorable to patentability which the party proposes to contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions not affecting the merits may be required to be settled before appeal considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of jurisdiction to the Board (§41.35 / §41.64)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdiction over the proceeding passes to the Board upon transmittal of the file, including all briefs and examiner's answers, to the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Board finds the file incomplete or noncompliant, it may relinquish jurisdiction to the examiner or take other action; Director may sua sponte remand prior to entry of decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments after filing an appeal but before filing brief (§41.33(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed after filing an appeal and prior to the date a brief is filed may be admitted as provided in §1.116.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.116 for scope and conditions of admitting amendments after final action but before or on same date as appeal filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments after filing a brief (§41.33(b)-(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed on or after the date of filing a brief may be admitted only to cancel claims (when cancellation does not affect scope of other pending claims) or to rewrite dependent claims into independent form; all other amendments filed after filing an appeal will not be admitted except as permitted by specified sections (§§41.39(b)(1), 41.50(a)(2)(i), 41.50(b)(1), 41.50(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-permitted amendments are excluded; limited exceptions permit admission in connection with certain Board orders or remands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits or other evidence filed after appeal (§41.33(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or other evidence filed after the appeal and prior to the brief may be admitted if the examiner determines it overcomes all rejections under appeal and good and sufficient reasons are shown why it was necessary and not earlier presented; other affidavits/evidence filed after appeal generally will not be admitted except as permitted by specified sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict showing required; other evidentiary submissions after appeal are tightly limited and governed by the cited sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time and fee requirement for filing an appeal brief (§41.37(a)-(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant must file a brief within two months from the date of filing the notice of appeal and the brief must be accompanied by the fee set forth in §41.20(b)(2). Failure to file the brief with the fee within the period results in dismissal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time periods are extendable only under the specified provisions (§1.136 for patent applications, §1.550(c) for ex parte reexamination) as noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents and order of an appeal brief (§41.37(c)(1) / §41.67(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief must contain under appropriate headings and in the indicated order: (i) Real party in interest; (ii) Related appeals and interferences (with copies of decisions in an appendix); (iii) Status of claims and identification of claims appealed; (iv) Status of amendments after final rejection; (v) Summary of claimed subject matter with specification and drawing references and identification of means-plus-function/step-plus-function elements with corresponding structure/material/acts in the specification; (vi) Grounds of rejection to be reviewed on appeal; (vii) Argument treating each ground/issue under separate headings with legal/record citations; (viii) Claims appendix; (ix) Evidence appendix (copies of evidence entered by examiner and where entered in the record); (x) Related proceedings appendix (copies of decisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellants unrepresented by registered practitioners need only substantially comply with many of the items. For inter partes, similar content rules and specific references to columns/lines in the specification apply. Reference to unentered evidence is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means-plus-function and step-plus-function identification (§41.37(c)(1)(v) / §41.67(c)(1)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each independent claim and each dependent claim argued separately, every means-plus-function and step-plus-function must be identified and the corresponding structure, material, or acts described in the specification must be set forth with specification (page/line or column/line) and drawing references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precise citation to the specification and drawings is required to show corresponding structure for 35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument format and waiver for grouped claims (§41.37(c)(1)(vii) / §41.67(c)(1)(vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments must address each ground/issue and be supported by citations; each ground/issue must be under a separate heading. When multiple claims subject to the same ground are argued as a group, the Board may select a single claim to decide for the group; failure to separately argue grouped claims constitutes a waiver of separate patentability arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statement merely pointing out what a claim recites will not be considered an argument for separate patentability. Claims argued separately or as a group must be placed under subheadings identifying the claim numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on new or non-admitted matter in briefs (§41.37(c)(2) / §41.41(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief or a reply brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, or any new or non-admitted affidavit or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.116 and §41.33 for limited treatment of amendments and evidence filed after final action or after appeal; briefs containing new matter risk being refused consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncompliant briefs — opportunity to amend and dismissal consequences (§41.37(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a brief does not comply with the requirements, appellant will be notified of reasons for non-compliance and given time to file an amended brief; failure to file an amended brief within the set period or to overcome all reasons for non-compliance will result in dismissal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict compliance enforced; notifications provide a non-extendable cure period as indicated elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's answer content and possibility of new ground (§41.39(a)-(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary examiner may furnish a written answer explaining the invention, references relied upon, and grounds of rejection; an examiner's answer may include a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a new ground is included, appellant has two months to either reopen prosecution (request withdrawal of appeal via reply under §1.111 with or without amendment/evidence relevant to the new ground) or maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief addressing each new ground (without amendments or new evidence). Failure to timely act risks sua sponte dismissal as to the claims subject to the new ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits and non-extendability for replies to examiner's answer (§41.39(b) / §41.41 / §41.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant must within two months from the examiner's answer exercise the options related to new grounds; a reply brief may be filed within two months of the examiner's answer; extensions under §1.136(a) are not applicable to these reply periods (but §1.136(b) may provide limited relief as noted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reply briefs must follow brief requirements and may not include amendments or new evidence; if a reply brief is accompanied by amendments/evidence it will be treated as a request to reopen prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's response to reply brief and supplemental answers (§41.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: After receipt of a compliant reply brief the primary examiner must acknowledge receipt/entry and may withdraw the final rejection and reopen prosecution or may furnish a supplemental examiner's answer responding to new issues; a supplemental examiner's answer may not include a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a supplemental answer is furnished, appellant may file another reply under §41.41 within two months of the supplemental answer; time extensions are not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing request and timing (§41.47(a)-(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: An oral hearing should be requested only when necessary or desirable; to request, file a separate paper captioned 'REQUEST FOR ORAL HEARING' accompanied by the fee in §41.20(b)(3) within two months from the date of the examiner's answer or supplemental answer. If not timely filed, the appeal will be decided on the briefs without an oral hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals decided on the briefs will receive the same consideration as those with oral hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing conduct and limitations (§41.47(d)-(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an oral hearing is held, a date will be set and notice given; oral argument will ordinarily be limited to twenty minutes for appellant and fifteen minutes for the primary examiner unless otherwise ordered. Appellant argues first and may reserve time for rebuttal. At the hearing, parties may only rely on evidence previously entered and present arguments that were relied upon in the brief or reply brief, except upon a showing of good cause to rely on a new argument based on a recent relevant Board or Federal Court decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary examiner may participate in argument. The Board may decide a hearing is unnecessary even if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decisions: affirmance, reversal, remand, and new grounds (§41.50)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may affirm or reverse the examiner's decision in whole or in part on grounds/claims specified; affirmance on any ground specified constitutes a general affirmance except as to reversed grounds. The Board may remand to the examiner. If the Board includes in its opinion grounds not involved in the appeal, it may state these as a new ground of rejection (not final for judicial review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the Board makes a new ground, appellant within two months must either reopen prosecution (submit amendment/new evidence for reconsideration) or request rehearing addressing the new ground with particularity. A new ground is binding on the examiner unless overcome by amendment/new evidence of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment in conformity with Board opinion (§41.50(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may include an explicit statement of how a claim may be amended to overcome a specific rejection; appellant has the right to amend in conformity therewith, and such an amendment will overcome the specific rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner may reject the so-amended claim provided the rejection constitutes a new ground of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board orders for additional briefing and compliance (§41.50(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may order appellant to additionally brief any matter it considers of assistance; appellant will be given a non-extendable time period to respond and failure to timely comply may result in sua sponte dismissal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such orders must be complied with strictly within the non-extendable timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing procedure and limitations (§41.52)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant may file a single request for rehearing within two months of the original Board decision stating with particularity points believed misapprehended or overlooked; arguments not raised in the briefs and evidence not previously relied upon are not permitted except as allowed (good cause for new arguments based on recent decisions or new arguments responding to a new ground of rejection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No second rehearing requests except in narrow circumstances; decision on rehearing incorporates earlier opinion and is final for judicial review except as noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action following decision (§41.54)
rubrics_metrics.description: After decision by the Board, the proceeding will be returned to the examiner, subject to appellant's right of appeal or other review, for such further action by appellant or the examiner as required to carry the decision into effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board remands and further prosecution follow the normal examiner procedures; remand decisions may not be final for judicial review until appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter partes: amendments and evidence after appeal (§41.63)
rubrics_metrics.description: In inter partes appeals, amendments filed after filing an appeal that cancel claims may be admitted where cancellation does not affect scope of other pending claims; all other amendments filed after appeal will not be admitted except as permitted by §41.77(b)(1). Affidavits or other evidence filed after appeal will not be admitted except as permitted by reopening prosecution under §41.77(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter partes appeals have stricter post-appeal amendment/evidence rules; consult §41.77(b)(1) for permitted circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter partes: timing for briefs and no-extension rule (§41.66)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant's brief must be filed no later than two months from the latest filing date of the last-filed notice of appeal or cross appeal; the time for filing an appellant's or amended brief may not be extended. Respondent's brief must be filed within one month after service of appellant's brief and cannot be extended. Rebuttal briefs (by any appellant) may be filed within one month of the examiner's answer. No further submissions will be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict, non-extendable deadlines in inter partes proceedings; any noncompliant additional submissions are treated per §1.939.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter partes appellant's brief content and formalities (§41.67)
rubrics_metrics.description: An inter partes appellant's brief must be signed by the appellant or authorized attorney/agent, accompanied by the requisite fee (§41.20(b)(2)), and contain (under headings and order) real party in interest; related appeals/interferences (with decisions in an appendix); status of claims (owner must identify rejected claims appealed; requester must identify claims with determinations favorable to patentability being appealed); status of amendments; summary of claimed subject matter with column/line references and means/step-plus-function identification like ex parte; issues to be reviewed; argument with separate headings; claims appendix; evidence appendix (copies of evidence entered and statements where entered).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party requester cannot propose a new ground of rejection unless withdrawn by the examiner during prosecution and the requester hasn't had opportunity to propose it; arguments/authorities not included in permitted briefs will be refused unless good cause is shown.
